title: Chapter exercises with progressive difficulty
learningObjectives: Explain the concept or reference contract.
Trace the example and justify its behaviour.
Identify relevant assumptions and edge cases.
Apply the skill in a documented exercise.

understand.concept: Progressive exercises begin with focused recall or tracing, then move to small modifications, independent implementation, edge-case handling and integrated problems. Each task should specify inputs, outputs, constraints and expected behaviour.
understand.whyItMatters: A difficulty progression builds confidence while ensuring that learners move beyond copying examples to independent problem solving.
understand.analogy: Treat a reference or learning task as a contract that states what is expected and how success is checked.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace the exact C standard or library specification.

explain.narrative:
Progressive exercises begin with focused recall or tracing, then move to small modifications, independent implementation, edge-case handling and integrated problems. Each task should specify inputs, outputs, constraints and expected behaviour.

Use authoritative declarations and documentation, state assumptions explicitly and verify behaviour with focused examples. Where the implementation or C version matters, record it.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.explanation: A beginner task may trace this function; an intermediate task may handle empty input and NULL policy; an advanced task may generalize the predicate through a callback.

practise.guidedTask: Create three exercises for the same function at increasing difficulty.
practise.independentTask: Design a chapter exercise set with explicit constraints, sample cases, hints and a rubric.
hints: Progression should increase reasoning demands, not merely code length.
Provide hints that guide reasoning without giving away the complete solution.
